title: LumenForge retail ops kickoff journal
content:
Kickoff call notes (raw) - LumenForge retail ops integration
Date: 2025-11-05 call w/ Ana Morales (LumenForge) + ops/infra team
Attendees: Ana M (LumenForge PM), Diego (infra), Priya (Redwood SE), Tom A (Redwood infra), Kai N (RLSE eng), client security lead (Jen)

Summary / ask
- LumenForge wants an on-prem / VPC-hosted Redwood deployment for checkout assistant (intent recognition + upsell suggestions) across 1200+ stores.
- Primary constraints: sub-200ms 95th token-latency on 99% of interactive requests at peak store concurrency; EU data residency for EU stores; audit logs retained 7 years for regulated products.
- Traffic pattern: peak 7–9pm local, bursty at registers; expected concurrent requests ~30 QPS per region (initial), average prompt length ~200 tokens, occasional long (700 tokens) for batch analytics.
- Goal: Replace LexaAI endpoint (current) without degrading checkout latency or changing client-side experience.

Technical details gleaned
- POS environment: stores run local edge servers with 4–8 vCPU + 32GB RAM; they'd prefer edge inference for critical path but willing to route to regional VPC for heavy ops.
- Network: intermittent 50–100ms RTT to regional data center from stores; some stores have 300ms+ spikes (rural).
- Security: KMS in customer tenant, HSM available; strict egress policy — cannot send PII to third-party cloud. Logs must be exportable to client SIEM (Splunk) via push/fwd.
- Existing model profile: LexaAI-small equivalent, 7B-ish, currently CPU-quantized. They are open to a quantized GPU variant but want cost estimate and quality baseline.

Initial Red flags / gotchas
- If we do regional routing only, rural stores with 300ms spikes will see total latency > 500ms; unacceptable. Need local fallback (small model) or local caching.
- Client uses templated prompts heavily — repeated prefix with order metadata. Opportunity for prefix/KV caching to cut token cost and latency.
- Audit log retention 7 years: confirm Redwood Console export + retention policies; verify data residency (logs stored within EU for EU stores).
- Payment/PCI surface: ensure Redwood runtime never materializes card numbers in logs or telemetry; must scrub tokens or have an allowlist for PII redaction at the SDK/proxy layer.

Engineering notes / hypotheses
- Hybrid strategy: edge microservice (local, CPU-only lightweight LL model e.g., distilled 1.3B) for 95% of quick intents + regional Redwood VPC for full model and complex completions. Fallback policy: local first, then regional if confidence low.
- KV caching: push repeated prompts' prefixes to an in-store Redis cache; Redwood runtime can use prefix caching to avoid reprocessing common tokens — estimate 35–50% token reduction.
- Batching/throughput: for checkout UX we must disable large batching windows; continuous batching with max-latency cap 15ms for micro-batch is necessary.
- Quantization: propose int8 or awq int4 candidate for regional GPU pool; need A/B quality evals vs Lexa baseline on a 3k-prompt test set.

Data/QA plan
- Collect 3k anonymized prompts (no card data) from Lexa logs to form a baseline eval set. (Owner: Ana)
- Run quality/latency/regression evals: output similarity, token counts, hallucination metrics. (Owner: Priya + Kai)
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% over 48–72 hour windows per region; auto-fallback if error rate > 3% or P95 latency > 200ms. Feature flag gating in client. (Owner: Tom A + client infra)

Operational asks we must confirm asap
- Can LumenForge host a small inference container on their in-store servers? If yes, what OS/container runtime? (asked: most run Ubuntu 20.04 LTS; need details)
- SIEM integration: Splunk endpoints + auth method. They want logs streamed in near realtime.
- KMS/HSM: will they give us an external KMS endpoint or expect us to integrate with their KMS? Need key rotation window & contact.
- Data residency map: list of store locations by country to plan regional VPCs. (Ana to send CSV)

Open questions / TODOs
- (Ana) Send sample prompt logs (anonymized) and list of top 200 templated prefixes — due 2025-11-08.
- (Tom) Prototype small local inference container (1.3B distilled) and smoke test on store VM image by 2025-11-18.
- (Priya) Draft initial evaluation rubric + test harness for comparison vs Lexa by 2025-11-12.
- (Kai) Estimate cost difference for regional quantized GPU vs current Lexa costs (per-1000-requests) by 2025-11-14.
- (Security) Confirm telemetry redaction rules and add scrubbing in SDK proxy before logs leave store. (Jen assigned)

Notes from client concerns (verbatim fragments)
- "We cannot afford slow checkout windows — even 100ms extra means longer lines."
- "Our legal team flags anything leaving the EU — logs and inference calls."
- "If the replacement produces worse suggestions we'll revert immediately; rollback needs to be trivial."

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Request: Ana to upload anonymized prompt CSV + store-country map. (Priya to follow up Wed 11/06)
- Redwood: spin up local container PoC and share install checklist for in-store ops. (Tom/Kai)
- Security: draft redaction checklist + example scrub rules and get client signoff. (Jen/Priya)
- Scheduling: book 30m follow-up next Wed with client infra to align on network ports/firewall rules.

Longer-term notes / thoughts
- If local inference proves stable, we could offer a managed image update pipeline (binary deltas) and signed updates to stores; productize as "Redwood Edge Appliance" later.
- Consider a small elastic Dedicated pool per major region to handle batch analytics from stores (nightly heavy runs) separate from interactive traffic.

Random capture:
- Prompt example (anonymized): "SUG|order12345|ITEMS[...template...]|ask: upsell-suggest -ctx customer_profile_age:45"
- Typical session: 2 quick intents + 1 upsell suggestion -> avg tokens generated 60

Slack refs: #client-lumenforge, #onprem-deploys, convo id: p1234-llm-migrate

If anything here is unclear ping me — Priya. I want to convert this into a tidy implementation checklist once we get the prompt CSV and network specifics.

-- end raw notes --
